title: operator-logbook-snapshot-2026-05-02
content:
Operator logbook snapshot - overnight shift (UTC)

Shift window: 2026-05-02 22:00 UTC -> 2026-05-03 06:00 UTC
On-call: Asha Patel
Relayer/secondary: Miguel Santos (00:30-04:30 UTC)

Purpose: quick, scannable handoff + raw chronology + preliminary runbook notes for a recurring low-latency regression we saw in the early morning window. This is intentionally informal — timestamps, commands, and TODOs to follow-up in the morning.

Executive summary:
- Between ~2026-05-03 01:10 and 01:42 UTC we observed a sustained 300–400ms P95 latency increase on the hosted-text-generation route (api/v1/generate) in us-west-2 region. Token throughput unchanged. Error rates stayed <0.1% but timeouts began creeping up for longer sequences.
- Immediate mitigations: rolled back an autoscaler policy tweak (reverted max-batch-size change), manually drained one pool that was at >80% GPU memory pressure, and enabled a conservative prefork multiplier to reduce cold-starts. These reduced P95 back to target within ~12 minutes.
- Possible root causes: aggressive batch sizing + KV-cache thrash due to a traffic burst with longer prefix sequences, combined with a new kernel selection path on a small subset of instances (see SRE-1724).

Play-by-play timeline (raw):
- 01:07 UTC: Alert - latency-penalty-usw2 P95 > 200ms (Grafana alert). First pager to on-call.
- 01:09 UTC: Correlate: GC and CPU metrics look normal; GPU memory pressure high on pool-3a-spot-*. Memory evictions spikes on NV cache.
- 01:11 UTC: Noticed rollout of autoscaler-config v2.6 (deployed ~00:58 UTC) which increased allowed batch-size from 64 -> 96 for model-e. Ticket/PR ref in linked_artifacts.
- 01:13 UTC: Mig initiated lightweight traffic-sampling using k6 proxy to check sequence length distribution — median unchanged but 95th shifted from 128 -> 420 tokens.
- 01:16 UTC: Executed revert of autoscaler-config to v2.5 on the canary pool (commands: infractl deploy-config autoscaler-config:v2.5 --pool canary-usw2). Observed immediate reduction in batch formation time.
- 01:19 UTC: Drained instance gpu-03a-07 (infractl instance drain gpu-03a-07) — this instance showed repeated KV-cache evictions and an anomalous kernel selection log (kernel-selector flagged fallback-to-generic). Marked for postmortem.
- 01:23 UTC: Enabled prefork multiplier override to 1.2 (runtime-config set prefork.multiplier=1.2 --scope region:us-west-2). Purpose: reduce cold-start jitter while batches settle.
- 01:30 UTC: P95 trending down; alerts cleared at 01:39 UTC.
- 01:42 UTC: System stabilized; resumed normal monitoring cadence.

Immediate actions taken (what we did):
- Rolled back autoscaler-config change on canary then rolled to full pool after verifying behavior.
- Drained and quarantined gpu-03a-07 for deeper investigation (kernel selection logs + nv-cache behavior captured).
- Enabled prefork multiplier override regionally as a temporary safety net.
- Increased sampling for sequence-length telemetry from 1% -> 10% for 12h to help model/batching correlation.

Observations + notes to follow-up:
- gpu-03a-07 logs show repeated "kv_cache_eviction_count" spikes coincident with the traffic burst. Need to pull nv-cache kernel traces and compare to other instances in pool.
- Kernel-selector logged fallback events for a specific op-fusion path. This path was touched by the runtime opt changes in model compilation for model-e earlier this week. Possible mismatch with newer driver behavior on that instance type.
- Autoscaler-config v2.6 increased batch-size for throughput reasons; but with long-tail sequence lengths it amplifies per-request latency variance. Need a better workload-aware batch sizing strategy.

Runbook draft (rough, for SRE review):
- Trigger: P95 > 200ms for 5m on api/v1/generate AND GPU mem pressure > 70% on >20% of pool instances.
- Immediate steps (first 15 minutes):
  1) Check sequence-length histogram (dash: SRE -> gen/seq-lens). If 95th > 300 tokens, reduce max-batch-size to 64 temporarily.
  2) Check kernel-selector fallback rates (log pattern: "kernel-selector: fallback"), if fallback_count > 5/min then quarantine instance(s).
  3) If mem-evictions > threshold, drain affected instance and mark host for kernel/driver triage.
  4) Enable prefork.multiplier override to 1.2 regionally if cold-start variance observed.
- Escalation path: if P95 remains >200ms after 20 minutes, escalate to Model Ops (Harper Liu) and Runtime dev (team oncall: infra-runtime). Create a quick incident channel and assign SRE-ops lead.

Open questions (for morning):
- Is there a recent driver/firmware push that landed on only a portion of the pool? (Harper to check infra release notes and instance patching logs.)
- Should batch-sizing policy be dynamic by sequence-length percentiles rather than a single static max? (Product/Model input required.)
- Can we add a targeted KV-cache warmup for long-prefix traffic to reduce eviction spikes?

Action items & owners (small list):
- Asha: collect gpu-03a-07 full kernel logs and upload to /internal/sre/artifacts/gpu-03a-07-20260503.log (due 2026-05-03 12:00 UTC).
- Miguel: run a replay test with long sequences against canary with autoscaler v2.6 toggled to reproduce latency pattern (due 2026-05-03 14:00 UTC).
- Harper: confirm instance patching matrix and report any driver deltas across pool (due 2026-05-03 10:00 UTC).
- Product: (ask via linked ticket) evaluate dynamic batching prototype for sequence-length aware policy; initial feasibility doc requested by 2026-05-09.

Notes to incoming shift (quick bullet list):
- Watch gen P95 in us-west-2 for next 24h; sampling increased to 10% so dashboards will be noisier.
- Avoid rolling autoscaler-config changes without a 30m canary observation on seq-length heavy traffic windows.
- If you see kernel-selector fallback spikes, immediately tag instance and quarantine — we observed cross-instance contagion effect in the past.

Personal notes / scratchpad (informal):
- Mig: remind infra-runtime we need a repeatable repro harness for kernel-selector fallbacks. A synthetic mixed-length workload should surface this quicker than prod sampling.
- Asha: sleep now, will do the log upload in the morning. If page hits again, wake me.

Appendix: useful commands and dashboards (quick copy-paste)
- Query: grafana -> gen/latency/p95?orgId=1&var-region=us-west-2
- Kernel logs: infractl logs instance gpu-03a-07 --since 2026-05-03T00:00:00Z > /tmp/gpu-03a-07.log
- Drain instance: infractl instance drain gpu-03a-07 --reason "kv-cache-evictions"
- Revert config: infractl deploy-config autoscaler-config:v2.5 --pool all-usw2

End of logbook snapshot.

-- Asha (on-call), 2026-05-03 04:15 UTC
